channel.title: Hastings Daily
channel.description: Local news for Hastings, St Leonards, Rye, Bexhill and Battle, three times a day.

item.title: Hastings MP marks one-year anniversary of the beach 'beads' pollution incident
item.description: It is a year since Southern Water admitted responsibility for the millions of plastic beads that washed up on the beaches at Hastings, Camber Sands and at Rye Harbour Nature Reserve, and Hastings MP Helena Dollimore has marked the anniversary of what is thought to be one of the biggest plastic pollution incidents on the South Coast of England.

item.title: Police seek man over theft of cash from Bexhill M&S
item.description: Sussex Police is seeking a man in connection with the theft of cash from the Marks and Spencer store in Ravenside Retail Park, Bexhill.

item.title: Rye Town Clerk honoured with the town's highest civic award
item.description: Richard Farhall has been made an Honorary Freeman of the Ancient Town of Rye, the town's highest civic award, in recognition of his 26 years of service as Rye Town Clerk.

item.title: St Leonards Frost Fair returns on November 28 with Snow Queen parade
item.description: The St Leonards Frost Fair returns on Saturday 28 November with a parade of colourful fairy-tale characters, led by the Snow Queen, processing through the streets.

item.title: Two Bexhill Colonnade kiosks available to let for new businesses
item.description: Two kiosks at the Grade II listed Colonnade in Bexhill are available to let for new businesses, offered through commercial property agents Dyer & Hobbis.

item.title: Update: Rother to consult on 2027/28 budget with £2.72m in reserves
item.description: Rother District Council has launched its public consultation on the draft 2027/28 revenue budget, which runs until 5pm on Wednesday 16 December 2026. The authority said it faces a funding gap of £1.2 million while planning to spend £38m on services, and council leader Doug Oliver urged residents, businesses and community groups to have their say.

item.title: Hastings council budgets £1,937,861 for St Mary in the Castle in 2026/27
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has budgeted spending of £1,937,861 on the Grade II* listed seafront building St Mary in the Castle in the 2026/27 financial year, with the majority set to come forward as capital spending.

item.title: Update: Rother to consult on 2027/28 budget with £2.72m in reserves
item.description: Rother District Council has launched its public consultation on the draft 2027/28 revenue budget, which runs until 5pm on Wednesday 16 December 2026. The authority said it faces a funding gap of £1.2 million while planning to spend £38m on services, and council leader Doug Oliver urged residents, businesses and community groups to have their say.

item.title: Two men charged with murder of Bexhill cyclist
item.description: Two men have appeared at Lewes Crown Court, charged with the murder of a Bexhill cyclist, Sussex Police have said.

item.title: Councillor calls 500-home Bexhill plan a 'disaster zone waiting to happen'
item.description: A Bexhill town councillor has described proposals for a potential 500 new homes in the town as a 'disaster zone waiting to happen'.

item.title: Donations top £10,000 for Isfield farm shop after raid
item.description: Donations totalling more than £10,000 have flowed in to help a family farm in Isfield after thieves ransacked its shop, the owners said.

item.title: On this day, 1918: The Armistice reaches the East Sussex papers, 1918
item.description: When news of the Armistice reached Britain on 11 November 1918, newspapers in East Sussex reported on the joy and the solemn reflection of the county.

item.title: Residents to have say on East Sussex supported housing strategy
item.description: People in supported housing across the district can have their say on how it should improve, Rother District Council has said.

item.title: Bexhill Leisure Centre named UK Active Awards finalist
item.description: Bexhill Leisure Centre has been named a finalist for Regional Centre of the Year at the UK Active Awards, one of the leisure industry's leading national award programmes.

item.title: Little Common Library marks annual volunteer lunch
item.description: Volunteers and supporters came together in Bexhill for Little Common Library's annual fish and chip lunch, its chairman Connor Winter said.

item.title: Plans for 42 new homes by St Leonards' Bannatyne's Spa Hotel
item.description: Outline permission has been submitted to build up to 42 homes on land at Bannatyne's Spa Hotel in Hastings Road, St Leonards, according to the latest Hastings Borough Council planning applications.

item.title: Battle Bonfire 2026: 'Guy Feaux' effigy takes a swipe at AI
item.description: Battle High Street became a 'river of fire' on Saturday night as people turned out for the town's annual bonfire celebrations, the Hastings Observer reported.

item.title: Nineteen-year-old opens her own beauty salon in Bexhill
item.description: Grace Guenigault, 19, has opened her own beauty salon in Bexhill, the Hastings Observer reported.

item.title: Rye Bonfire named among the UK's best Bonfire Night displays
item.description: The Rye and District Bonfire has been named among the best Bonfire Night displays in the country, The Argus reports.

item.title: Hastings brothers set for Nepal peaks for veterans' charity
item.description: Two brothers from Hastings are heading to the Himalayas to raise money for a local veterans' charity.

item.title: Westfield player Michael Rwabigwi called up for Rwanda
item.description: A player at a tenth-tier English football club has been called up to represent his country.

item.title: On this day, 1883: Electric street lights trial switched on in Hastings
item.description: This week in November 1883, a trial of electric street lights in the town was switched on.

item.title: Police launch manhunt for man wanted for recall to prison
item.description: Police have launched a manhunt for a man wanted for recall to prison and are asking anyone who sees him to call 999.

item.title: St Leonards' Becky Palmer wins Christmas tree flinging at Catsfield
item.description: A 27-year-old from St Leonards has won the women's title at the Christmas tree flinging contest at Catsfield Christmas Tree Farm near Battle.

item.title: Two Sussex police officers charged over assault of detained man
item.description: Two Sussex Police officers have been charged with assault occasioning actual bodily harm over an incident involving a man detained in hospital under the Mental Health Act, according to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC).

item.title: Swansea Sound to open tour at The Piper in St Leonards
item.description: Swansea Sound, who feature members of Heavenly and Talulah Gosh, are to kick off their tour in St Leonards at The Piper on 13 November.

item.title: Camber Sands holiday park ranked among worst in UK
item.description: Camber Sands Holiday Park, near Rye, has been named one of the lowest-rated holiday parks in the country.

item.title: St Leonards and Hastings properties sell at Clive Emson auction
item.description: A mixed-use property at 32 Kings Road, St Leonards, has been sold before the auction in one of the latest Clive Emson Auctioneers sales, which listed 174 lots across southern England.

item.title: Local band raises £3,000 for Warming Up the Homeless
item.description: A group of local musicians have raised around £3,000 for Warming Up the Homeless in the last couple of years by giving their CDs away free and encouraging audiences to donate to the charity instead.

item.title: Hastings swimmer plots route to 2028 Channel crossing
item.description: Hastings swimmer Sarah Milne has completed an endurance training camp in Dover with The King's Swimmers and, in her latest diary for the Hastings Independent Press, says she is now preparing for a solo Channel crossing attempt in 2028.

item.title: Fire-hit St Leonards convent site goes to auction at £1.7m
item.description: A former convent in St Leonards that was damaged in a major fire earlier this summer is going on the market, with a guide price of £1.7 million and a potential major housing scheme for the land.

item.title: The Plough in Rye named among Britain's best pubs
item.description: A pub in Rye has been named among the best in the country, with recognition for what the guide calls an unpretentious country pub.

item.title: Hastings runner to take on 55-mile ultramarathon in jeans
item.description: A 21-year-old from Hastings is about to take on one of the country's toughest challenges, and he is doing it in denim.

item.title: MP joins launch of Hastings & St Leonards Poppy Appeal
item.description: Helena Dollimore, the MP for Hastings, Rye and the villages, has joined veterans and volunteers at the launch of this year's Hastings & St Leonards Poppy Appeal, held in Tesco, raising money for veterans and their families.

item.title: Cabinet to consider £1.5m playground funding on Monday
item.description: More than £1.5m to improve playgrounds across the town is set to be considered at the council's Cabinet meeting on Monday evening.

item.title: Plans for up to 125 homes at Robertsbridge mill site
item.description: Proposals to build up to 125 homes on the Hodson's Mill site in Robertsbridge are set to go before Rother District Council's planning committee on Thursday, 12 November. The plans come from Homes England, the government's housing and regeneration agency.

item.title: Call for interest in future use of Sandhurst Recreation Ground
item.description: Hastings Borough Council is asking sports clubs, groups and organisations to register their interest in the future of Sandhurst Recreation Ground. The council wants to know how much demand there is for the sports pitches, which organisations would like to use the site, and whether it could be managed or developed by the community.

item.title: Ada the Asda car park fox has been relocated to a safer home
item.description: Ada, the friendly fox that made her home in an Asda car park in Hastings, has been moved to a safer place by a wildlife charity. The fox had become well known for approaching shoppers, begging for food and trying to climb up people's legs.

item.title: Bexhill mayor celebrates new school councillors at Glenleigh Park Primary
item.description: Glenleigh Park Primary Academy in Bexhill hosted a special assembly to celebrate student leadership, with the Mayor of Bexhill, Cllr Memish Huseyin, in attendance. The visit marked the appointment of the school's newly elected school and eco councillors, following an election campaign that involved all pupils.

item.title: Have your say on renewal of five gated paths in Hastings and St Leonards
item.description: Hastings Borough Council is asking for views on plans to renew gating orders for five public rights of way in Hastings and St Leonards.

item.title: Hole Park near Rye promises a top Christmas tree crop after summer drought
item.description: One of the Rye area's longest established Christmas tree growers is promising a top-quality harvest for the second year in a row.

item.title: Seagull artist's gull-version masterpieces on show in Crown pub
item.description: Hastings artist Bill Greenhead, known for his cartoon-style paintings of chip-stealing seagulls, has an exhibition in the Snug bar of the Crown in Hastings Old Town.

item.title: Driver jailed for 13 months after 104mph police pursuit ended in ditch
item.description: A disqualified driver has been jailed for 13 months after leading police on a 31-minute pursuit through Hastings, Winchelsea and Rye that ended in a ditch in Iden.

item.title: Labour ends cooperation with Greens on 11 councils
item.description: Labour has withdrawn from power-sharing agreements with Green councillors in 11 local authorities, including Arun, Lewes and Wealden district councils in Sussex, over the party's ‘Zionism is Racism’ policy.

item.title: Sculptor Leigh Dyer's steel fins go on sale at At Sea
item.description: The metal sculptor behind several well-known works around Hastings has opened a new line for sale at the At Sea gallery in the Old Town.

item.title: Man pleads guilty to shoplifting across Hastings and Rother
item.description: A 45-year-old man from Winchelsea Beach has been charged in connection with a series of shop theft offences across Hastings and Rother.

item.title: Update: White Rock Gardens could get covered padel and tennis courts
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has announced it is in line to receive £1.3million of investment funding to construct a new covered tennis and padel centre, with a projected overall cost of £1.8million and the council pledging £500,000 match funding.

item.title: West Hill Lift closed for urgent surveys and repairs
item.description: The West Hill Lift has been closed for essential surveys and repairs, according to the Hastings Independent Press.

item.title: BFI film course sees 18 young people make their first film in St Leonards
item.description: A group of 18 young people under 19 have taken part in a six-day film course in St Leonards, making an original short film from scratch as part of the BFI Film Academy South East Introductory Course.

item.title: GP link worker helping Hastings residents with long-term conditions get active
item.description: Active Hastings' specialised 'Link Worker' is helping residents with long-term health conditions become more active, bridging the gap between healthcare and community-based activity, according to the Hastings Independent Press.

item.title: Hastings Draft Local Plan: Convent site open for comment until 12 November
item.description: The deadline for the public to comment on the Hastings Borough Council's Draft Local Plan is Thursday 12 November, and one of the most argued-over parts of it is what happens to the Convent of the Holy Child Jesus in Lower Bohemia.

item.title: From Hastings to the Royal Albert Hall: Count Us IN set to perform
item.description: Fifty-one young musicians from Hastings and St Leonards will take the stage at the Royal Albert Hall on 10 November as part of the Music for Youth Proms.

item.title: Hastings care home rated 'Good' across all five CQC areas
item.description: Mountside Care Home in Hastings has been rated 'Good' in all five areas assessed by the Care Quality Commission.

item.title: Bexhill family featured in Chestnut Tree House hospice film
item.description: The family of a six-year-old Bexhill boy who died of a brain condition has featured in a new film as part of a campaign to show the vital role of hospices.

item.title: Council to seek group to take lease of Hollington Community Centre
item.description: East Sussex County Council is looking for a local group to take on the lease of Hollington Community Centre in Old Church Road, after saying the building needs significant investment to bring it back into good repair.

item.title: Work begins on 27 'luxury flats' development in St Leonards
item.description: Work has started on a scheme of 27 flats in St Leonards. Scaffolding is going up and the first foundations are being built on a West Hill Road site, according to the Hastings Observer.

item.title: 'Write by the River' poetry exhibition opens at Rye station
item.description: A new poetry and artwork exhibition called 'Write by the River' has opened at Rye railway station. It features poems and illustrations about the area's waterways, including the River Rother and River Tillingham.

item.title: Storms strip Pett Level beach, exposing 1940s sea wall
item.description: Storms Austen and Boelo have stripped away large sections of Pett Level's shingle beach defences, exposing for the first time in decades an old 1940s stepped concrete sea wall and a tarmac service road that had been buried beneath the shingle, according to the Hastings Independent Press.

item.title: Update: Hastings Castle to get £288,500 from Historic England for repairs
item.description: Following the £288,500 Historic England award and a £200,000 contribution from the council, the first phase of conservation works at Hastings Castle has begun, with specialist contractors removing vegetation from sections of the castle walls and the motte. The works are due to be completed by 16 November.

item.title: Hastings' last wooden fishing boat 'Felicity' to be restored and displayed in Rock-a-Nore
item.description: The last surviving wooden fishing boat from Hastings is to be restored and put on permanent display after a fund-raising campaign reached its target of £5,000. The 'Felicity', RX58, will be displayed on the piece of land opposite the Dolphin pub in Rock-a-Nore Road.

item.title: Self-storage operator opens 44th site on Sedlescombe Road, St Leonards
item.description: Self-storage specialist Cuboid Self Storage has opened its second site in Sussex, on Sedlescombe Road in St Leonards-on-Sea. The facility opened on 1 November and is the company's 44th site nationwide, joining its existing facility in Shoreham.

item.title: Devolution measures to bring £8m to Sussex and Brighton
item.description: Last week's budget included measures to give devolved local government in England a bigger share of its own tax revenues, the Hastings Online Times reports.

item.title: Hastings council to consider Age Friendly strategy for older residents
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has drawn up an Age Friendly Hastings Strategy and Action Plan, with proposals to make the town more accessible and inclusive for people aged 50 and over.

item.title: Car wash owner sentenced over illegal workers
item.description: A car wash owner in Hastings has been sentenced after illegal workers were repeatedly found at his business, Sussex Police said.

item.title: Ark Alexandra CCF wins three honours at Lord-Lieutenant's Awards
item.description: Ark Alexandra Academy's Combined Cadet Force had a triple win at the Lord-Lieutenant's Awards Ceremony, held at Lancing College and attended by senior military personnel and civic representatives from across the region.

item.title: Police increase patrols in Eldridge Way area of St Leonards
item.description: Police said they are increasing patrols in and around Eldridge Way, St Leonards, near The Ridge, following reports of anti-social behaviour from local residents.

item.title: Police make 18 weekend arrests in Hastings and Rother
item.description: Sussex Police made 18 arrests in Hastings and Rother between 30 October and 1 November, a spokesperson said.

item.title: Rye station to close from 3pm for bonfire celebrations
item.description: Southern has announced that Rye railway station will be closed from 3pm on the day of the town's bonfire celebrations, Saturday, 14 November, until the regular start of service the next day, Sunday.

item.title: Former St Leonards church becomes community hub with weekly market
item.description: A former church in St Leonards has become a thriving community hub, hosting a popular weekly market and serving as a venue for concerts and events.

item.title: Update: Developers reveal bid to build 120 new Hastings homes
item.description: Catesby Estates and Rurban Estates are now inviting people to have a say on the proposals before finalising them and submitting planning applications to Hastings Borough Council and Rother District Council. The development would include approximately 120 new homes, of which 30 per cent would be affordable housing, a care home, a new landscaped public open green space and children's play area. Many readers have voiced concerns about traffic on The Ridge and pressure on local services, according to the Hastings Observer. Feedback can be shared via a consultation at www.catesby-hastings.co.uk.

item.title: Free parking at Hastings council car parks in December
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has agreed plans to provide free parking at its council-owned car parks on specific dates in the run-up to Christmas.

item.title: Bexhill councillor calls parking permit charges 'extortionate'
item.description: A Bexhill town councillor has branded the price of residential parking permits in the town 'extortionate and over the top'.

item.title: Toilets top of residents' list in £21.5m Pride in Place survey
item.description: New toilets have topped the list of improvements residents want in Hastings, after MP Helena Dollimore asked how the £21.5 million of Government Pride in Place funding should be spent.

item.title: One East Sussex reorganisation to proceed, with four Lewes wards moving to Brighton
item.description: The Government has announced it is minded to proceed with local government reorganisation in East Sussex, Hastings Borough Council has said.

item.title: Charity raises £4,000 to save Bexhill Hospital stroke rehabilitation service
item.description: Becky, Sarah and Owen from the #DoItForJosh charity met the team at Bexhill Hospital’s Irvine Unit on Monday to mark the continuation of a vital local stroke rehabilitation programme.

item.title: Cooden Beach Golf Club seeks permission for homes on part of its course
item.description: Cooden Beach Golf Club is seeking planning permission to build housing on part of its course on Cooden Sea Road, according to an application to Rother District Council.

item.title: Westfield says farewell to Christmas Lights co-founder Ken Munday BEM
item.description: Westfield, outside Hastings, has paid its respects to Ken Munday, who was awarded the British Empire Medal for his services to the village.

item.title: On this day, 1896: This week in 1896: first moving pictures shown on St Leonards Pier
item.description: This week in 1896, the first moving pictures to be shown in Hastings and St Leonards were seen on St Leonards Pier, the local record shows.

item.title: Man convicted of 18 offences after shop thefts in Hastings
item.description: Tom Marchant, 44, of no fixed address, has been convicted of 18 offences after a series of shop thefts in Hastings, Sussex Police have reported.

item.title: Bird deaths spark campaign to remove netting in Hastings and Rother
item.description: A new local campaign is calling for safer ways to manage birds around buildings after three incidents in which birds became trapped in netting.
